title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Likely elemental powders of Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe and Co blended to form a lightweight high-entropy alloy precursor
recollection.intervention: Spark-plasma sintering or hot-press sintering at different temperatures (e.g., 800-1100 °C) to consolidate the powder
recollection.structure: Single or dual FCC/BCC solid-solution phases whose grain size and phase fraction vary with sintering temperature; higher temperature producing denser, coarser grains and reduced porosity
recollection.mechanism: Temperature-dependent diffusion and solid-solution stabilization typical of high-entropy alloys; higher temperature promotes atomic diffusion, grain growth and possible phase transformation from dual-phase to single-phase structure
recollection.results: Trend of rising density and mechanical strength (yield ~350-550 MPa, hardness ~200-320 HV) up to an optimal temperature, then strength drops due to grain coarsening; electrical/thermal conductivity and corrosion resistance improve with densification but plateau or decline after excessive growth.

score.note: The recollection tentatively identifies spark-plasma sintering and a plausible temperature range, but misses the specific optimum of 1000 °C. Its structural and mechanistic descriptions are generic, omit the uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases and passive-film/Cl− blocking mechanism, and partly conflict with the reported BCC starting phase. The estimated hardness is far below the actual 1235.5 HV, and none of the density, oxidation, or corrosion values are recalled.
